key_insight: A disease-centric vision-language pretraining framework for 3D CT improves semantic alignment by combining a hybrid CNN-ViT visual encoder, disease-level contrastive learning, and diagnosis-aware prompting.
clinical_relevance: The approach aims to make zero-shot CT diagnosis and report generation more reliable by learning disease-specific imaging-language links from radiology reports.
method: 3D CNN replaces ViT patch embedding to better capture local anatomy while keeping global attention.
Learnable query tokens extract disease-level semantics from full reports for contrastive alignment with CT features.
Diagnosis-aware prompts use real clinical phrases and disease prototypes to reduce pretraining-inference mismatch.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art results on CT-RATE (84.4% AUC, +5.1%) and Rad-ChestCT (75.4% AUC, +5.4%), with a larger +9.8% AUC gain on a 60-disease benchmark.
watch_item: Performance depends on high-quality report supervision and benchmark-specific prompt design, so external validation and robustness across sites/scanners remain important.
paper_title: Disease-Centric Vision-Language Pretraining with Hybrid Visual Encoding for 3D Computed Tomography
